The preservation of natural resins and organic pigments demands an archival environment shielded from erratic thermal flux and unfiltered luminescence. Within the lower gallery, specimens undergo continuous optical inspection under controlled monochromatic wavelengths to detect microscopic fissures before crystallization sets in.

![Plate Alpha](plate-1.jpg "Planche Alpha")

Early cataloging protocols relied heavily on manual transcription, noting specific gravity, solubility in rectified spirits, and refractive indices against standardized quartz plates. The initial ledger entries, preserved across vellum leaves, record the gradual transition from raw fossil copal to purified dipterocarp distillates collected along equatorial fault lines.

![Plate Beta](plate-2.jpg "Planche Beta")

Subsequent analyses confirm that volatile terpenic fractions dissipate within the first sixty lunar cycles of application. What remains is a hard, vitrified lattice adhering firmly to the ground layer.

> An archival environment shielded from erratic thermal flux.

Obviously very efficient.
